citation.authors: Raz O, Steinvil A, Berliner S, Rosenzweig T, Justo D, Sasson A, Shapira I
citation.title: The effect of two iso-caloric meals containing equal amounts of fats with a different fat composition on the inflammatory and metabolic markers in apparently healthy volunteers

population.description: 54 apparently healthy non-obese staff members (38 women, 16 men) of a Tel-Aviv hospital, no recent acute or chronic inflammatory disease, no anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive drugs or steroids; each served as their own control on two meal mornings 3 weeks apart. Screening was for inflammation and drugs only; no glucose-tolerance or metabolic screening was reported, and the group's fasting insulin (about 25 uU/mL, HOMA-R about 5) is not that of a metabolically screened group, so status is unselected although the authors call the volunteers 'apparently healthy'. Age 41.7 and BMI 25.9 are printed with '± 3.1' and '± 0.9', which the Statistical analysis section calls standard errors; SD left null because SE x sqrt(54) would give 22.8 y and 6.6 kg/m2, and the paper's own Table 2 (age 39.7±4.0 n=15, 44±2.2 n=39; BMI 24.8±1.0, 27.1±0.9) implies SDs of about 14 y and 4-6 kg/m2, so the whole-group age figure does not fit it. Age and BMI are for all 54, not by sex.

protocols.name: women_fasted
protocols.description: Women (n = 38): the fasting (0 h) sample of the SFA-meal morning of Table 3. Venous blood drawn at 8 A.M. after a 12-hour overnight fast (Methods, Study design and Laboratory methods), before the meal; the meal itself is not entered (its carbohydrate and protein grams are not printed). Entered as a 30-minute fasted run-in ending at the 08:00 draw: start_hour = 8.0 - 0.5 = 7.5, prefast_hours = 12 - 0.5 = 11.5, sample read at minute 29-30; run-in length and the arithmetic are mine.
